title: Developer Sandbox LivePair - Auth & Environment Walkthrough
summary: AE + SE ran a live developer sandbox session showing Redwood SDK quickstart (Python/TS), auth flows (API keys, GCP Workload Identity), console onboarding, and Optimize suggestions. Discussed production constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: provide sandbox invite, security pack, pricing sketch, and schedule a short perf benchmark next week.

Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-26
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Verdant EM), Mark (Verdant Platform), Sofia (Verdant ML), Jackson (Verdant PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): quick live pairing onboarding, walkthrough of SDK auth flow, console tour, optimize suggestions; next steps include sandbox invite and perf run.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see Priya, Mark, Sofia, Jackson — awesome. We're gonna do a quick livepair, show the Python and TypeScript quickstarts, then hop into the Console and Optimize recommendations. Typical format — we'll demo, answer questions, then wrap with next steps.

[00:28] Priya: Sounds good. Timebox is tight, we have an infra meeting at 3:55 so we'll try to keep it to 50.

[00:35] Liam: Great, I'll share my screen — starting from the repo and the quickstart notebook. First, auth options: API key for dev, Workload Identity for GCP, and on-prem we can wire KMS/HSM.

[01:02] Mark: Quick Q — our policy requires keys to rotate and to come from our KMS. Can we integrate that into CI/CD?

[01:12] Maya: Yep, Redwood supports KMS-backed secrets and rotation; we'll send our KMS integration guide, but in the sandbox you'll see a short example using GCP KMS and workload identity.

[01:35] Liam: Ok opening the Python notebook. Cell 1: pip install redwood-inference. Cell 2: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... (we typed a redacted key). Then small snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(); client.complete("Write a test blurb") — response streams.

[02:05] Sofia: Nice — is there a TS snippet too? We have a couple of Node microservices.

[02:15] Liam: Yep, here's the TS example — import {Redwood} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood(); await client.generate({prompt: '...'}); We showed both streaming and non-streaming variants.

[02:49] Priya: I noticed in examples online you mention prefix/KV cache — how does that work with our multi-tenant app?

[03:05] Liam: Good question, the KV cache is per-route and can be scoped by token or user id. For multi-tenant you'll typically set cache keys with tenant prefixes, so prefixes don't collide. Also, the Console shows cache hit rates per route.

[03:34] Mark: On performance — we need 80th percentile latency under 200ms for short completions (<=128 tokens). Can hosted meet that or do we need Dedicated?

[03:50] Liam: For that SLO we usually recommend Dedicated for sustained traffic; hosted can meet it for bursty low-traffic but for consistent 200ms SLOs at scale Dedicated or private in-region is safer. We can run an initial perf to validate.

[04:12] Priya: What's the cost delta roughly between hosted and dedicated?

[04:20] Maya: Rough sketch: hosted is pure usage-based; Dedicated has a monthly reserved capacity but reduces per-token unit cost for high throughput. We'll send a pricing sketch with ballpark numbers after this.

[04:45] Sofia: Any workarounds if we want to keep data in our VPC?

[04:52] Liam: Yes, Redwood Private supports a VPC-private control plane and on-prem agent for air-gapped setups. The Private option includes KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. For many customers we do a hybrid: control plane in our infra but model serving in their VPC.

[05:20] Jackson: For pilot scope, what minimal telemetry do we get out of the box? We want token-level costs and per-route latency.

[05:30] Maya: Console provides token breakdown, per-route/model dashboards, traces, and we've got tracing hooks you can attach to your logs. You'll also see feature flags for rollouts and canary.

[05:55] Liam: Ok jumping to Console — here is the routes page, showing a sample route with traffic. See the Optimize tab suggests batching=16 and 8-bit quantization for this route because the sequence lengths are short.

[06:25] Priya: How invasive is quantization on quality? We cannot accept hallucinations increasing.

[06:34] Liam: There's a tradeoff. For retrieval-heavy prompts quantization often has minimal impact; for instruction-following it can change behavior. Optimize gives model + quantization recommendations per workload and highlights expected quality delta. We recommend running our evaluation harness (we'll include example eval prompts in the notebook).

[07:05] Maya: We'll point you to a small benchmark sheet we use internally — it's a spreadsheet we can share with you with suggested tests. Link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/verdant-pilot (placeholder link)

[07:25] Mark: Is the streaming API compatible with websocket realtime? We plan to use partial token streaming in our chat UI.

[07:34] Liam: Yes streaming is via chunked HTTP or websockets depending on client. We showed the TS example using EventSource for streaming tokens to the client.

[08:00] Priya: Could you show the SDK error handling pattern quickly? Our stack wants idempotent retries and deadline propagation.

[08:12] Liam: Sure — example: client.generate({timeout: 5000}) with retry-policy wrapper. We highlighted retry-after headers and idempotency keys for generation endpoints.

[09:00] Maya: Quick qualification: what's your timeline and stakes for pilot?

[09:08] Priya: We're looking to run a 6-week pilot starting in mid-September with the intent to move to production by Q1 if metrics look good. Security and auditability are gating factors.

[09:20] Maya: Great — that fits our typical pilot cadence. We'll provide SOC2 docs and the KMS guide.

[10:02] Sofia: Any gotchas migrating from our current internal infra? We use a self-hosted transformer inference service and have examples of sharded KV cache.

[10:18] Liam: Biggest friction points are differences in tokenization defaults (we use byte-pair variants) and cold-start behavior. We can run a compatibility run; sometimes a model variant or quantization profile will make behavior more similar.

[10:50] Mark: About model variants — do you have smaller low-cost models we can fall back to when load spikes?

[10:58] Liam: Yes we support model routing policies: route to a cheaper variant when latency or budget thresholds are hit. Console can show fallback events in the trace. You can define per-route fallback policies.

[11:30] Priya: Any reference on retention? Our compliance team needs logs for 7 years or scrubbed PII.

[11:40] Maya: Redwood supports configurable retention and redaction rules and audit logs that can be exported. For strict PII rules you can enable private deploy and local logs only. We'll include these details in the security pack.

[12:05] Liam: Now livepair demo step — I'm going to run a simple perf script from the notebook to the hosted sandbox (we had a dev key loaded). Running 250 requests with concurrency 5.

[12:35] (typing and shell noises)

[13:05] Liam: Results are streaming in: p50 ~160ms, p90 ~210ms for short completions in hosted dev. This is a small sample — we'll run a larger dedicated script for your expected load.

[13:30] Jackson: Those numbers look promising, but we need to validate under our access patterns.

[13:42] Maya: Agreed — that's why the follow-up perf run is on the action items. We'll provide the script and check-in.

[14:05] Priya: One more question on auth: can we map Redwood roles to our SSO groups? We use Okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning.

[14:15] Liam: Yes SSO + RBAC is supported via SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles and limit access to certain routes or models.

[14:40] Sofia: For the SDK, is there built-in support for batching multiple small prompts into one request (we want to decrease per-token overhead)?

[14:50] Liam: SDK supports client-side batching and then the runtime does continuous batching server-side too. Optimize will recommend batching config like request-aggregation and shard sizes.

[15:15] Maya: Ok we're nearing the end of the demo. Quick recap: we'll send the sandbox invite, starter notebook, KMS and SSO guides, a pricing sketch, and the perf runbook. Liam will prepare the perf script and benchmarks.

[15:35] Priya: Sounds good. Also please include the evaluation harness examples so our ML team can run quality regressions.

[15:45] Liam: Yup we'll include unit evals and a short tutorial on hooking up your prompt set to Redwood Optimize.

[16:00] Mark: Any quick notes on cost controls? We need hard budget limits for pilot stage.

[16:10] Maya: Console supports per-route caps and quota alerts; you can also set auto-fallback to cheaper model variants when cost thresholds are hit.

[16:35] Jackson: All right that's it for us, thanks.

[16:40] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and the security pack.

[16:48] (meeting ends, recording stops)

Post-call notes: shared links — Dev notebook: https://redwood.app/dev-notebooks/verdant-sandbox (placeholder); Security pack: https://redwood.app/security-pack; Benchmark spreadsheet shared as view-only link.

Transcript notes: occasional ASR mis-hearings in proper nouns (Verdant vs Verdant Systems) and timestamps approximate.
